skill.name: pptx
skill.description: Create, edit, inspect, and validate PowerPoint presentations using HTML conversion, OOXML editing, thumbnail grids, and template-based workflows.
skill.summary: PowerPoint workflow support for creating, editing, validating, and analyzing PPTX files.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, JavaScript template literals, and OOXML namespace URIs. Confirmed risks include unsafe Office ZIP extraction, external converters processing user-provided files, and sudo dependency commands. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unsafe extraction of Office ZIP archives
remediation.suggestion: Validate every ZipInfo member path before extraction, reject absolute or parent-directory paths, and extract only expected OOXML members.
Run LibreOffice and Poppler in a sandbox with resource limits, fixed arguments, and user confirmation for untrusted files.
Remove sudo install commands from agent workflows and document dependencies as manual setup steps for the user.

content.value_statement: PowerPoint work often needs precise layout checks, template reuse, and XML-level repairs. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical workflows for PPTX creation and editing.
actual_capabilities: Creates new PPTX decks from HTML slide designs using PptxGenJS.
Extracts presentation text and layout inventory for template analysis.
Unpacks PPTX files for direct OOXML inspection and edits.
Rearranges template slides by duplicating, deleting, and reordering slides.
Generates thumbnail grids to inspect slide layout and visual quality.
Validates edited OOXML before repacking a presentation.
limitations: Requires local dependencies such as PptxGenJS, Playwright, LibreOffice, and Poppler for full workflows.
Complex animations, embedded media behavior, and advanced PowerPoint effects may need manual review.
OOXML edits can corrupt a deck if validation steps are skipped.
Some workflows process local files and should run only in a trusted workspace.

use_cases.title: Build a new sales deck
use_cases.description: Create a polished PPTX from an outline, then validate layout with generated thumbnails.

use_cases.title: Adapt an existing template
use_cases.description: Analyze template slides, select matching layouts, and replace placeholder text safely.

use_cases.title: Repair a damaged presentation
use_cases.description: Unpack the PPTX, inspect OOXML relationships, edit XML, and validate before repacking.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a new presentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 6-slide PPTX about [topic]. Use a clear visual style, generate thumbnails, and fix any visible layout issues.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an existing deck as a design source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [template.pptx], create a slide inventory, and recommend which template slides fit my outline.

prompt_templates.title: Edit Slide Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Modify an existing presentation while keeping formatting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [deck.pptx] with this replacement content. Preserve layout, validate text fit, and return the edited file.

prompt_templates.title: Repair OOXML Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for corrupted or invalid PPTX files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Unpack [deck.pptx], inspect OOXML validation errors, repair the affected files, repack the deck, and explain each change.

output_examples.input: Create a short investor update deck from a project brief.
output: A PPTX file with title, market context, traction, roadmap, and next steps slides.
A thumbnail grid used to verify spacing, readability, and visual hierarchy.
A concise note describing design choices and any remaining manual checks.

output_examples.input: Use a branded template to make a customer proposal.
output: A template inventory that maps slide indices to layout purposes.
A revised proposal deck using selected template slides in the requested order.
A validation summary covering text replacement and layout checks.

output_examples.input: Fix a PPTX where one slide relationship is broken.
output: An unpacked OOXML inspection summary identifying the broken relationship.
A repaired PPTX that passes the included validation workflow.

best_practices: Generate thumbnail grids after every major layout change.
Keep all source files and generated outputs inside the active workspace.
Validate OOXML immediately after each manual XML edit.
anti_patterns: Do not skip validation before repacking an edited PPTX.
Do not reference template slide indices without checking the actual slide count.
Do not use manual bullet characters when a real list structure is expected.

faq.question: Can this skill create a PowerPoint file from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses an HTML-to-PPTX workflow with PptxGenJS for positioned slide content.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing PPTX?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports template workflows and direct OOXML edits for existing presentations.

faq.question: Does it need external software?
faq.answer: Some workflows need local tools such as LibreOffice, Poppler, Playwright, Sharp, and PptxGenJS.

faq.question: Can it preserve template formatting?
faq.answer: It can preserve formatting when replacement text is mapped to the correct template shapes.

faq.question: Can it validate a deck after editing?
faq.answer: Yes. The included OOXML tools validate relationships, content types, namespaces, and schema issues.

faq.question: Is this suitable for sensitive decks?
faq.answer: Use it only in a trusted local workspace because workflows read and write presentation files.
